# Project Constitution
Identity: constitution-v1. Current.
- Mature practices require evidence of applicability to current conditions.
- Public concepts have one meaning, owner and lifecycle.
- Responsibilities and state authority have explicit owners.
- Complexity must serve an actual present contract and consumer, considering behavior, maintenance, security and compatibility.
- New changes converge debt; retained old consumers have applicable boundaries and exit conditions.

Identity: project-change-contract-v1. Concern set: project-concerns-v1.

A reviewed technical-rule revision may be proposed in the original contribution and promoted only through the existing lifecycle. Planning itself does not write shared current.

baseline_files.docs/architecture/README.md:
# Current architecture
Identity: current-v2. Active.
OfferWriter owns config revisions and per-account eligibility. InventoryWriter owns a finite shared stock count. Current OfferWriter touches one common control revision for each account even when configuration is unchanged.
baseline_files.docs/requirements/README.md:
# Applicable requirements
OFFER: independent accounts may establish eligibility under stable configuration. For a concurrent disable, the revision observed by an eligibility transaction must remain valid at commit; same-account duplicate creation must stay idempotent. There is no cross-account reward count or inventory cap.
INVENTORY: the last unit must be sold to at most one account; two accounts contend for the same finite stock. Keep that global invariant. No exact production latency/throughput SLO is supplied.
baseline_files.docs/design/README.md:
# Current behavior and constraints
Offer configuration has revision 9 throughout the synthetic interleaving. Account A and B write disjoint eligibility records but both CAS control revision. The stock counter is a different current authority, not part of Offer eligibility.

candidate_design: The new online offer entry reuses unchanged offer coordination and an existing bounded retry loop. Candidate A preserves that design. Candidate B removes cross-account control writes but has not specified how concurrent disable is observed at commit. Candidate C removes stock coordination too. Assess current applicability, alternatives and evidence limits.
